SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK FP-14: FHIRPath — §6.2 Comparison. Test these items: > (Greater Than), < (Less Than), <= (Less or Equal), >= (Greater or Equal). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.evidence: Both native C++ and forced Python fallback return true for `true > false` and `truth > falsity`. Section 6.2 defines comparison only for strings, integers, decimals, quantities, dates, datetimes, and times; Boolean comparison should not produce an ordered Boolean result.
issues.root_cause: Both backends let host-language Boolean ordering leak into FHIRPath comparison handling even though Section 6.2 does not define ordering for Boolean.
issues.resolution: Native C++ now throws FHIRPathSpecError for same-type Boolean comparison operands, and Python fallback raises FHIRPathError. Public result UDFs catch these and return empty/NULL.
issues.verified_in: Fresh FP-14 probe, test_comparison_parity.py, native fhirpath.test sqllogictest, full conformance 2822/2822

issues.evidence: Both native C++ and forced Python fallback return row-resilient empty for `(1 | 2) < 3`, `1 < (2 | 3)`, and `arr < b`, but `fhirpath_is_valid()` returns true. Section 6.2 requires both operands to be singleton collections and says the evaluator throws an error if either side has more than one item.
issues.root_cause: Comparison operators returned an empty collection directly for multi-item operands instead of raising the singleton error required by Section 6.2, so literal multi-item cases looked valid to fhirpath_is_valid().
issues.resolution: Native C++ and Python fallback now raise typed singleton errors for multi-item comparison operands. Public result UDFs remain row-resilient, while literal multi-item validity checks now return false.
issues.verified_in: Fresh FP-14 probe, test_comparison_parity.py, native fhirpath.test sqllogictest, full conformance 2822/2822

issues.evidence: Both native C++ and forced Python fallback produce Boolean results for calendar duration keyword vs UCUM duration comparisons above seconds: `1 year > 1 'a'` returns false, `1 month <= 1 'mo'` returns true, and similar week/day/hour/minute cases return false. Section 6.2 says calendar durations and definite quantity durations above seconds are incomparable and should return empty.
issues.root_cause: Quantity comparison reused broad unit conversion tables for calendar duration keywords and UCUM duration codes, missing the Section 6.2 rule that those duration families are incomparable above seconds.
issues.resolution: Added mixed calendar/UCUM duration guards in Python FP_Quantity.compare and native C++ quantity comparison. Above-second mixed duration comparisons return empty; seconds and milliseconds still compare.
issues.verified_in: Fresh FP-14 probe, test_comparison_parity.py, native fhirpath.test sqllogictest, full conformance 2822/2822
